question:
An organization only holds Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses (no P2 and no Microsoft Entra ID Governance add-on). The compliance team wants to require every user to read and accept a legal terms-of-use document, enforced through Conditional Access, before they can sign in to any application.

Can this be achieved with the organization's current licensing?

options.text: Yes — Conditional Access terms of use (ToU) attestation is included with Microsoft Entra ID P1 and does not require P2 or the Governance add-on
No — terms of use requires Microsoft Entra ID P2 at minimum
No — terms of use is only available as part of the Microsoft Entra ID Governance add-on
Yes, but only if the organization also purchases the Microsoft Entra Suite

explanation:
Unlike many other identity governance capabilities, **Conditional Access terms of use (ToU) attestation** is included starting at **Microsoft Entra ID P1** — it does not require P2 or the Microsoft Entra ID Governance add-on. An administrator uploads the ToU document and targets it in a Conditional Access policy requiring users to view and accept it before being granted access.

**Why not the other options:**
- **"Requires P2 at minimum"** and **"only in the Governance add-on"** — both overstate the licensing requirement; ToU is explicitly one of the few identity governance-adjacent features already available at the P1 tier, unlike entitlement management, access reviews, or PIM, which do require P2 or Governance.
- **"Only with Microsoft Entra Suite"** — the Entra Suite includes ToU (since it includes everything in Governance and more), but it is not required to use ToU — P1 alone is sufficient.
